name: dark-eincol-1
context:
EINCOL ROUND 1 ON DARKMATTER, step 5: handed to an evaluator I do not control, with my reasoning withheld from the claims themselves.

─────────── THE QUESTION ───────────

Which intervention in a running gravitational system EXPANDS the set of reachable futures, and can a player STEER that expansion or only trigger it? Your own earlier lead named both halves: "Energy Injection and Mass Injection can expand the reachable phase space" and "the screening must distinguish between expanding the space and creating chaos."

─────────── WHAT WAS MEASURED BEFORE ANYTHING WAS GENERATED ───────────

Stage 0 of the physics, all green: Lyapunov 0.098 per sim-second (10.2s prediction horizon against a ~30s round); spatial extent in z is 19-30% of x, a genuine thick disc; energy drift NON-directional at 17% skew over 1500 steps; the system moves on its own, mean |dx| 7.09 over 400 steps.

Then a verb sweep, 6 seeds x 9 parameter levels x 600 steps, outcome = fraction of bodies still bound:

    verb      expansion (sd of outcome)   steerability (rank corr)   mean bound
    NONE            0.0000                      1.000                  0.764
    IMPULSE         0.0526                      0.653                  0.764
    MASS            0.0632                      0.983                  0.936
    DRAG            0.0838                      0.958                  0.927
    PIN             0.0414                      1.000                  0.801

TWO THINGS IN THAT TABLE ARE WRONG AND BOTH MATTER MORE THAN THE RANKING.

NONE scores steerability 1.000. With no intervention every parameter level gives an identical outcome, so variance is zero and the rank correlation is computed over tied ranks. A statistic that cannot vary with the thing it tests -- the fifth time this project has hit that signature.

DRAG scores the HIGHEST expansion, and drag is the textbook stabiliser. It tops the table because the metric measures LEVER STRENGTH, not state-space volume: a strong monotone dial with a wide range scores high on "spread of outcome across a parameter sweep" while doing the opposite of what the metric is named for.

─────────── THE DISTRIBUTION, WITH THE TAIL WORKED ───────────

    0.26  mass injection -- adds degrees of freedom rather than energy
    0.19  NOTHING expands; every verb is a convergence engine and Darkmatter is
          Chemical again with better graphics
    0.15  the expansion is in the OBJECTIVE, not the verb -- a scalar outcome has
          a one-dimensional reachable set by construction
    0.13  resonance, not force -- a small periodic nudge at an orbital frequency,
          so the currency is timing precision rather than magnitude
    0.10  expansion requires TWO interventions that interact
    0.08  expansion by SUBTRACTION -- removing a body opens configurations its
          own gravity forbade
    0.05  tidal disruption is the only real expander, and it lives entirely in
          the near-singular encounters the softening length exists to bound
    0.04  there is no state space to expand, only the OBSERVER's uncertainty

Tail work, with a structural analogy imported from a distant field: QUANTUM CONTROL THEORY. The reachable set of a bilinear control system is generated by the LIE ALGEBRA of its control fields -- one field reaches a submanifold, two fields with non-zero bracket reach the whole space. That gives a precise borrowed reason to expect a PAIR of verbs to do what no single verb can, and it predicts something falsifiable: interventions that COMMUTE (two impulses on one body along one axis) should add nothing, while non-commuting ones (an impulse plus a displaced mass drop) should compound.

─────────── FALSIFYING MY OWN FINDING, BOTH VERSIONS KEPT ───────────

CLAIM: mass injection expands the reachable state space while staying steerable, so it should be the primary verb.

Case it predicts, checked: best measured pairing, 0.0632 and 0.983. Holds.

Case it gets wrong, which I looked for hardest: DRAG out-expands it at 0.0838 and drag is unambiguously a stabiliser. Either drag really expands the reachable set -- physically false -- or the metric measures something else. It does.

CORRECTED CLAIM: mass injection is the only verb measured that is both a strong lever and reliably aimable. WHETHER IT EXPANDS ANYTHING IS NOT ESTABLISHED, because the metric conflates lever strength with state-space volume, and a vector-valued outcome with a volume measure is required before the word "expansion" is used again.

And a warning stronger than the ranking: mass injection and drag BOTH RAISE mean boundness (0.936 and 0.927 against 0.764 for no intervention). Every verb, and competent inaction, push the same way. That is the shape of a game with no tension in it.

─────────── WHAT THE ROUND CHANGED BEFORE ANY FACTOR WAS SCREENED ───────────

  1. expansion is not yet measurable; the word is not used again until a
     reachable-set volume over a vector outcome replaces sd-of-a-scalar;
  2. the softening length eps becomes a SCREENED FACTOR rather than a constant --
     it is the dial the tidal candidate turns and you already named it the
     cheapest Lyapunov remedy;
  3. verb PAIRS get screened, not just verbs, on the Lie-algebra argument;
  4. "hold it together" is probably the wrong objective.

55 candidate solutions were drafted against the four measured problems (design/dark-55.md), grouped by which problem each attacks rather than by feature.

questions.text: I am withholding the word 'expansion' until a reachable-set volume replaces spread-of-a-scalar. Is that the right correction, or is there a reason sd-of-outcome IS the right measure for a game, where what matters is how much the player can change the result rather than how many states exist?

The Lie-algebra argument predicts commuting interventions add nothing and non-commuting ones compound. Is that a legitimate import from control theory to an N-body game, or am I borrowing a formalism whose preconditions this system does not meet?

Every verb AND competent inaction raise boundness. I read that as 'no tension'. Is there a reading where a game whose verbs all stabilise is still a good game, and what would the objective have to be?
Of the eight distribution rows, which do you think I have mis-priced, and in which direction?

The tail row I took most seriously (tidal disruption, p=0.05) says the interesting behaviour lives exactly where the softening length suppresses it — so the fairness device and the depth source are the same dial. Is that a real tension or have I constructed it?
Was this EINCOL round executed properly — and what did it miss?
